data.raw_text:
Korean Air flight 903 Boeing 747-200 overran the runway at Manila Airport (MNL) and skidded to a halt near a highway, injuring 40 of the 378 people aboard on Tuesday 15 September 1981. There was no fire. Passenger injuries were sustained during the evacuation in the pitch darkness. As a result, the aircraft's nose blocked traffic on the service road of South Luzon Expressway.

The Korean airlines jetliner with 332 passengers and 20 crew members had made a one-hour stopover in Manila on a flight from Seoul, Korea to Zurich, Switzerland, via Manila and Bahrain

'It just skidded at the end of the runway,' said an air traffic controller, adding that the pilot seemed 'to want to abort his takeoff but it was no longer possible.'

After a rolling take-off and, moments after the first officer called V1 (80 knots), the flight engineer heard a "bang". He then saw the no. 4 engine EGT rise to maximum. The overheat limit light went on and he called out "engine fire". The pilot immediately initiated an abort but asymmetrical control problems arose, which compounded the effective use of the brake system.

The South Korean jet, carrying 378 passengers bound for Bahrain, stopped about 20 feet short of a busy expressway and blocked traffic on a service road,

Doctors at the airport clinic reported treating at least 40 passengers, including seven who were sent to a hospital with fractures. The rest, according to the doctors, suffered bruises.

This poor quality image is all that remains. The 747 was repaired and went on to fly with GATX leased to Nationair as N487GX until 1996. Painted into fictional "Quantum Airlines" livery for filming of a 1996 NBC miniseries titled "Pandora's Clock"

Boeing 747 - MSN 20493
Serial number 20493 LN:128
Type 747-230B
First flight date 17/03/1971
Status Scrapped.

Source - https://t.co/ntkCL382NV
